title: The letters, part 2: ל to ת

steps.intro: The other eleven letters, and five that change shape at the end of a word. Read each word from the right.

cards.title: The last eleven letters
body: Two of these are silent like alef: ע (ayin) carries a vowel but, as most people read today, makes no sound of its own.
ש is two letters with one shape: a dot on the right (שׁ) is sh, a dot on the left (שׂ) is s.

head: letter
name
sound
rows: p, or f without the dot

cards.title: Five letters with an end-of-word shape
body: At the very end of a word, five letters are written differently, most with a long tail down: כ becomes ך, מ becomes ם, נ becomes ן, פ becomes ף, צ becomes ץ.
They are the same letters with the same sounds. A final ך usually has no dot, so it sounds kh.

cards.title: Six letters that take the dot
body: Six letters can have the hard-sound dot: ב ג ד כ פ ת. Teachers remember them as “begad kefat”.
In the pronunciation used here only three of them change: בּ b and ב v, כּ k and כ kh, פּ p and פ f. With ג ד ת the dot makes no difference to the sound.
Five letters never take a dot to double them, because they are made in the throat: א ה ח ע and usually ר. Lesson 4 shows what that means for the vowels around them.

examples.en: silver: כּ is k, and the final ף is f
the dot in ת changes nothing

cards.prompt: Which is mem at the end of a word?
cards.explain: ם is final mem, as in שָׁלוֹם. ן is final nun, and ס is samekh.
With the dot on the right it is shin, sh. With the dot on the left (שׂ) it is sin, s.

cards.prompt: Match each letter to its sound.
Match each letter to its end-of-word shape.

cards.explain: From the right: ק (k), וֹ (o), ל (l): kol.
שָׁ (sha), לוֹ (lo), and final ם: sha-LOM.
מֶ (me), לֶ (le), and final ךְ (kh): ME-lekh.

steps.intro: Look for letters you know, and the end-of-word shapes.

cards.note: Four words: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” The first is יְהוָה, the LORD; the last ends in ר.
The blessing ends with שָׁלוֹם, peace, and its final ם.

items.en: the LORD (God's name, YHWH, read Adonai)
